# Palm et al.

Palm et al. is the author group behind a 2020 meta-analysis examining the effect of structured patient education on outcomes for patients with atrial fibrillation [^src1]. The study is cited extensively in the documentation of Indicator 8 (Struktureret patientuddannelse) within the AFDK-program (Atrieflimren i Danmark), a Danish national clinical quality program administered by Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram, where it serves as key evidence supporting the value of patient education as part of atrial fibrillation care [^src1].

Published in 2020, the meta-analysis pooled data from six studies — five randomized intervention trials and one non-randomized intervention study — covering a total of 2,007 patients [^src1]. The headline finding was that patients who received structured patient education experienced a 22% reduction in the combined risk of death and readmission compared to patients who received no such education, corresponding to a Risk Ratio of 0.78 (95% CI 0.63–0.97) [^src1]. This result underpins the rationale for structured patient education as a recommended component of atrial fibrillation treatment in the Danish AFDK program, which is built around the ABC Pathway model of integrated atrial fibrillation care (Avoid stroke, Better symptom control, Cardiovascular risk management).

The meta-analysis's findings were more mixed on secondary outcomes. Palm et al. did not find consistent conclusions regarding effects on health-related quality of life, anxiety, depression, and physical activity — some included studies found differences favoring patient education, while others found no differences between groups [^src1]. The authors also documented considerable heterogeneity in how patient education was delivered across the reviewed studies: session length ranged from 30 to 150 minutes per session, with follow-up occurring one to five times, roughly every two to three months, over periods extending up to 24 months [^src1].

The underlying literature review and meta-analysis methodology is described in the source material as based on a systematic literature review [^src1]. No relationships or additional claims involving Palm et al. beyond the meta-analysis itself are documented in the available corpus.
